points: On Monday, Sensex climbed 107.25 point to settle at 81,106.65, while the Nifty rose 58.25 points, or 0.23 per cent, to close at 25,044.65.
On 9 November, Indian equity markets extended their winning streak, although gains were modest compared with the sharp rally of the previous week.

The Nifty 50 rose 58.25 points to close at 25,044.65, holding above the crucial 25,000 mark, while the Sensex gained 107.25 points to settle at 81,106.65, its highest closing level in more than eight months.

points: Jharkhand chief minister Hemant Soren on Tuesday ordered a CBI probe into the death of 39-year-old tribal activist and leader, hours after the officer-in-charge of Pithoria police station was removed from his post following conspiracy allegations.
The tribal leader died allegedly by suicide on November 6 after going live on Facebook, accusing the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha-led government in the state and land brokers of harassing her.

items.title: New estimates show farm fires may be vastly undercounted in Punjab, Haryana
points: Farm fires in Punjab and Haryana hit their highest count of the season on Diwali even as new estimates put the scale of the problem vastly higher than what’s being counted.
Till October 28, INSAT-3DS, a weather satellite run by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), detected almost no farm fire in the two states.
From Oct 29 the count rose every day, from 18 to 447 on November 8, Diwali, and the daily average in the week to November 9 was 12.5 times that of the week to November 1.

On November 9, Jethva posted on X that the current farm fire figures were likely an undercount, with an empirical calculation using a combination of satellites and considering data till 4 pm: both Punjab and Haryana had likely logged closer to 34,000 farm…
Referring to data from the NOAA-20 VIIRS satellite (375m resolution) for both Punjab and Haryana from October 1-November 9, he said 4,089 fires were logged around 1:30pm.

items.title: Man Dies After Assault Over Rs 200 Temple Lights Payment In UP: Cops
points: A dispute over just Rs 200 paid for fixing lights at a temple during Diwali allegedly cost a 28-year-old physically challenged man his life after he was assaulted by a fellow villager in Uttar Pradesh's Pilibhit district, police said on Tuesday.

Khargsen was allegedly assaulted by a fellow villager, Siyaram, after he sought the return of the Rs 200, which he had paid for the temple lights but which were never installed, according to a complaint filed by his family.
The incident took place in Khajurha village.
The family has accused Siyaram of murder and demanded legal action against him.
According to the complaint, Khargsen had paid Siyaram Rs 200 during Diwali to fix lights at a temple.
When Siyaram allegedly failed to do so, a dispute broke out after Khargsen asked for his money back.
The family alleged that Siyaram assaulted Khargsen on Diwali, leaving him severely injured.

items.title: Man Arrested For Raping Woman, Filming Incident In UP: Cops
points: Police have arrested man for allegedly raping a woman and filming the act on his mobile phone in the Vrindavan Kotwali area of Mathura district after promising to secure her a house under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, officials said on Tuesday.
Vrindavan SHO Ashwini Kumar said the woman had applied for a house under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMA).
Some time later, she received repeated calls, with the caller claiming that her application had been approved and asking her to complete the paperwork.
The accused identified himself as Anil Kumar, the officer said.
On October 30, Kumar showed the victim a vacant plot, and claimed that the site had been approved for PMAY, under which she would receive a house for free.
On November 5, the accused called the victim to a guest house in Vrindavan, ostensibly to sign official documents and complete other formalities.
Based on the victim's complaint, Kumar was arrested on Tuesday under relevant sections of the BNS, the SHO said.

The officers include Block Development Officers (BDOs) and Circle Officers (COs), assistance engineers and junior engineers.

It is our duty to address everyone’s problems with sensitivity and promptness, and to ensure they receive justice,” Mr. Choudhary said while holding the ‘State-Level Sahyog Programme at Chief Minister’s Secretariat where 76 applications were received.
The ‘Sahyog’ camps are intended to address public concerns and ensure citizen satisfaction.

The initiative, which was launched for the first time by Mr. Choudhary, is part of the state government’s ‘Ease of Living’ under the ambitious ‘Saat Nischay-3’ programme aimed at delivering services at citizens’ doorsteps.

items.title: Producers welcome proposal for minimum sustainable price for tea
points: A Minimum Sustainable Price framework is therefore essential to bridge the widening gap between production costs and market realisations and to ensure the long-term sustainability of the industry,” said C.
K Dhanuka, Chairman, Dhunseri Tea and Industries.

Mr. Dhanuka added that a minimum sustainable price will help bring realisations in line with costs, so that the industry can accommodate wage revisions, protect employment and the competitiveness of Indian tea.
The proposal of implementing minimum sustainable price for tea have been made to Ministry of Commerce, which is yet to take a decision on the proposal, the stakeholders of tea industry said.

Suneel Singh Sikand, chairman of Indian Tea Association (ITA) called the recommendation for a minimum sustainable price is an important policy intervention towards addressing the structural challenges confronting the Indian tea industry.

items.title: Bombay High Court declines request for hearing each day in quota petitions for Maratha reservation
points: The Bombay High Court on November 5 declined a request to hear each day a set of petitions on a quota of 10% for Marathas in education and service under the State.
The court said hearing will continue on November 27.
The document in the case is PIL 30 of 2024, Bhausaheb Bhujangrao Pawar vs State of Maharashtra.
A petitioner moved the Bombay High Court against the SEBC Act, 2018, enacted by the government under Devendra Fadnavis.
That law gave Marathas 16% reservation in employment under the State and in education.
It held that justification did not exist for the 16% quota and reduced it to 12% in education and 13% in employment under the State.
In May 2021, a Bench of the Supreme Court struck down the SEBC Act, 2018.
It held that no circumstances justified reservation for Marathas beyond the 50% ceiling set by the 1992 Indra Sawhney judgment.

items.title: Shipping in New Crossroads After the US Mid-Term Election
points: According to Xclusiv, “for tanker markets, the implications are particularly interesting and potentially contradictory.
A gradual restoration of Middle Eastern exports could increase crude shipments, supporting VLCC and Suezmax employment.
Equally important is the potential restocking of commercial and strategic petroleum reserves following months of disruptions.
Replenishing inventories could temporarily generate substantial additional cargo volumes, supporting tanker utilisation and freight rates.
Normalisation through Hormuz and potentially the Red Sea could shorten trading distances, while reduced congestion, waiting times and diversions would release previously constrained tonnage.

October’s Washington–Moscow agreement facilitating Russian diesel exports, accompanied by partial sanctions waivers, demonstrated Trump’s prioritisation of energy affordability, although actual US deliveries remain uncertain.
The proposed extension of the Section 301 suspension until January 9th, 2027, could provide temporary relief for Chinese-built tonnage.
Any easing of US-China trade tensions could support containerised and dry bulk trade, while persistent restrictions would continue reshaping sourcing patterns and trading distances”, Xclusiv said.

items.title: Marine biodiesel demand to more than double by 2031 without IMO framework – IEA
points: Global marine biodiesel demand will rise from just under 1 billion litres/year (around 890,000 mt/year) in 2025 to nearly 2 billion litres/year (around 1.78 million mt/year) by 2031, the International Energy Agency (IEA) forecasts.
Even so, marine biodiesel would make up only 0.6% of total marine fuel use by 2031, the IEA says.
It will remain the main source of renewable energy in shipping, but it will account for just 1% of the growth in renewable energy use across all transport.
In that case, the IEA sees marine biodiesel use rising to more than 12 billion litres/year (more than 10.68 million mt/year) by 2031, or 4% of total marine fuel demand.
The framework would cover roughly 97% of the world’s merchant fleet by tonnage and set two tiers of targets for cutting the GHG intensity of ships’ fuel.

items.title: Xeneta Ocean Outlook 2027: Three Years, Three Shocks, And What Comes Next
points: For the third year running, 2026 began with an expectation that ocean container rates would soften.
In 2026 it was conflict in the Middle East and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
Spot rates from the Far East to the US West Coast are up 343% in October compared with 28 February, the day before the Middle East crisis began.
Every major fronthaul out of the Far East, to North Europe, the Mediterranean and the US East Coast, has seen triple-digit spot rate increases during 2026.
The Xeneta Ocean Outlook 2027 forecasts global average spot rates to fall 30% and long-term contract rates to fall 5% across the full year, measured against a Q3 2026 baseline.
Xeneta expects the global container fleet to grow 6.8% in 2027, with 2.9m TEU of new capacity arriving against 0.5m TEU scrapped.
Far East to US volumes rose 11% in August while inflation-adjusted US retail sales grew 1.9%.

China’s oil product exports, including gasoline, diesel, jet fuel and fuel oil, fell to 5.18 million ⁠tons in October from 7.16 million tons in September, but were up 14.6% from a year earlier, according to the data.

items.title: What the US midterm elections mean for energy
points: The language being used to describe the Democratic Party’s successes in the US midterm elections has been dramatic.

The results, which will make the Democrats the largest party in both the Senate and the House of Representatives, have been called “an extinction-level event” and “a Chernobyl-level disaster” for the Republicans.

President Donald Trump has pledged to use his veto power to block legislation he sees as harmful, and the Democrats will not have the two-thirds majorities in the Senate and House needed to override those vetoes.
Meanwhile, President Trump will retain the ability to implement his agenda through regulations and executive actions.

The most significant impact on President Trump’s actions is likely to come from increased scrutiny, as a result of Democrats taking control of Congressional committees and setting their own agenda for investigations.
In many areas, the Democrats will not want to force a sharp break with the Trump administration.

items.title: Hemant Soren recommends CBI probe into Nisha Bhagat’s death case
points: Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren, on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), recommended to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), the death case of Tribal leader and social activist Nisha Kumari Bhagat.
Nisha Bhagat on November 6, 2026, allegedly died by suicide in Jharkhand’s Ranchi shortly after going live on social media.
In her live broadcast she questioned the role of Hemant Soren’s government and certain individuals associated with land mafia, and the police.
Leader of the Opposition in Jharkhand Legislative Assembly Babulal Marandi on Saturday (November 7, 2026) demanded that the CBI look into the case.
“The CBI will now investigate the Nisha Bhagat case.
Orders have been issued,” Mr. Soren said in a post on X on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).
On Tuesday (November 10, 2026), the BJP’s Scheduled Tribe Morcha organised a torchlight procession in Ranchi.
She had also unsuccessfully contested Assembly election from Gumla seat in 2024 on the ticket of Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM).

items.title: Andhra Pradesh Cabinet clears policy frameworks to attract investments in AI, electronics, renewable energy
points: Chandrababu Naidu chairing the Cabinet meeting at the Secretariat in Amaravati on Tuesday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister N.

Chandrababu Naidu at the Secretariat on Tuesday, approved a series of proposals aimed at attracting investments in artificial intelligence, electronics, renewable energy, pharmaceuticals and manufacturing, besides taking decisions on infrastructure,…
The Cabinet approved the Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, Comics and Extended Reality (AVGC-XR) Policy 2026-31 and the Robotics and Physical AI Policy 2026-36.
It also cleared amendments to the Semiconductor and Display Fab Policy 2024-29.

Among the major investment proposals, the Cabinet approved an investment of ₹31,387 crore by AM Intelligence for a 512 MW green integrated AI data centre at Amanam in Bheemunipatnam mandal of Visakhapatnam district.

It also cleared a ₹4,000.20-crore Carbon Cosmo advanced materials manufacturing project at Naidupeta and land allotment to Dixon Technologies in Tirupati for an investment of ₹700 crore, sources said.

items.title: IndiGo Extends Suspensions Of Saudi Flights Amid Security Concerns
points: Citing ongoing safety and security evaluations, IndiGo has further extended the suspension of its commercial flight operations to four key destinations in Saudi Arabia, halting services to Jeddah and Madinah until November 21, and to Riyadh and Dammam…

Issuing a travel advisory on social media platform X, the airline stated that the operational adjustments were made following a comprehensive review of the security environment to ensure the safety of passengers and aircraft personnel.

"Following a careful assessment of the safety and security considerations, IndiGo has further extended the suspension of flights to and from Jeddah and Madinah until 21 November 2026 (inclusive), and Riyadh and Dammam until 30 November 2026 (inclusive),"…
The claims come amid renewed hostilities between Saudi Arabia and the Houthi rebels following the collapse of a 2022 truce that had paused fighting in Yemen's long-running civil war.

items.title: U.S. Formalizes Two-Month Extension of China Ship Port Fee Suspension
points: The Trump administration has formally extended its suspension of port fees targeting Chinese-built and Chinese-operated vessels for another two months, keeping the controversial measures on hold while Washington continues trade negotiations with Beijing.
The decision, published Tuesday in the Federal Register, extends the suspension through 11:59 p.m.
Eastern Time on January 9, 2027, with the measures potentially resuming January 10 unless further action is taken.

The extension took effect November 9, preventing the fees from returning following the expiration of an earlier one-year suspension agreed to under a trade deal between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in November 2025.

The measures were originally adopted in April 2025 and subsequently modified in October 2025 as part of a broader effort to counter China’s growing influence over global shipbuilding and maritime transportation.
The administration initially suspended the measures for one year beginning November 10, 2025, following a trade agreement between Trump and Xi.

items.title: Grandson can’t claim birthright in property after partition: Supreme Court

Dismissing a 29-year-old partition suit filed on behalf of a minor son who claimed half of his grandfather’s property, the court held that once the property devolved upon the grandfather’s Class I legal heirs and was divided among them, the joint…

A bench of justices Augustine George Masih and Sunita Agarwal, in a judgment delivered on November 6, held that the property inherited by the father under Section 8 of the Hindu Succession Act became his individual property, leaving no scope for his son to…

The court relied on its earlier ruling in Commissioner of Wealth Tax Vs Chander Sen (1986), which held that property inherited by a son under the 1956 Act devolves upon him in his individual capacity and does not automatically become Hindu undivided family…

items.title: CRPF set to acquire kamikaze drones for anti-insurgency operations
points: The Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) is set to acquire kamikaze drones for counter-insurgency operations, according to a document circulated to stakeholders on Monday seeking information, by month-end, on products they can supply.
According to the Quality Requirements (QRs) and Trial Directives circulated to stakeholders on Monday, the drones must carry two high-explosive warheads weighing a minimum of 1.5kg.
They must have a range of at least 15km and an endurance of at least 30 minutes of flight time while carrying the payload.

Raised in 2008, the Commando Battalion for Resolute Action (CoBRA) was deployed exclusively in anti-Naxal operations until May 2026, when, after India was declared Naxal-free, two battalions were deployed in Manipur.
People aware of the matter said sending more CoBRA battalions to Manipur and elsewhere is possible because the two battalions deployed there in May 2026 have delivered positive results.
The Bastar camp, where Modi celebrated Diwali , on Sunday, served as CoBRA’s operational launch pad for anti-Naxal operations deeper inside Bastar in recent years.

Visakhapatnam gets a facelift ahead of CII summit
points: Accompanied by GVMC officials, the Commissioner inspected arrangements at the main venue of the summit at Andhra University Engineering College Grounds on Tuesday.
As the nodal officer for the summit, the Commissioner said that works related to branding, landscaping, civil works, cleanliness and overall maintenance of the venue premises were being taken up.
Mr. Garg said that attractive plants were being planted along the central medians of major roads to enhance greenery across the city.
In addition works such as painting median grills with attractive colours, colouring roadside kerbstones and beautifying road dividers were also being undertaken.
Major junctions and traffic intersections are being enhanced with fountains, landscaping, greenery and modern decorative features to create a distinctive visual appeal, Mr. Garg said.
Works include improving greenery along Beach Road, developing central medians, maintaining cleanliness along roadsides and undertaking painting works.

The Commissioner stated that continuous sanitation activities were being undertaken along major roads, footpaths, beach surroundings, tourist destinations and important junctions across the city in view of the summit.
